findings.title: runSplitQuery mutates the caller's request.targets via applyTemplateVariables, causing double interpolation and corrupted queries when called from shard splitting
findings.body: runSplitQuery now maps request.targets through datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, ...). In the Loki datasource, applyTemplateVariables performs template variable interpolation in-place on the query object (it mutates query.expr and other fields, as evidenced by the shardQuerySplitting test mocks which do `query.expr = query.expr.replace(...)` and return the same object). runShardSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts:48-54) already interpolates the targets with applyTemplateVariables and then passes a subRequest built from the original `request` object into runSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts:163). Because the subRequest spreads `...request` but shares the same target object references, runSplitQuery interpolates the already-interpolated queries a second time. Consequences: (1) variables that expand to text containing `$`-like patterns or already-interpolated values can be re-interpolated, corrupting the LogQL expression; (2) `$__interval`/`$__range`-style variables are computed against the split sub-range on the second pass, producing wrong step/range values; (3) any variable whose interpolated output resembles a variable name gets expanded again. The shard-splitting path therefore executes queries with doubly-interpolated expressions. Fix: either make applyTemplateVariables return a copy (non-mutating), or have runSplitQuery/runShardSplitQuery operate on cloned targets so interpolation happens exactly once per query execution path.

findings.title: Shard-split sub-requests re-interpolate already-interpolated targets inside runSplitQuery, and the shard selector can be corrupted by the second interpolation pass
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery interpolates targets once (line 49-52) and groups them by their interpolated stream selector (getSelectorForShardValues on the interpolated expr). It then builds subRequest = { ...request, targets: interpolateShardingSelector(targets, shardsToQuery) } (line 154) and calls runSplitQuery(datasource, subRequest, ...) (line 163). runSplitQuery now unconditionally re-applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables to those targets (querySplitting.ts:296-299). Since interpolateShardingSelector injects a matcher like `__stream_shard__=~"20|10"` into the expression, a second interpolation pass runs template expansion over an expression that already contains interpolated content. If any template variable's value contains characters that look like LogQL or variable syntax, or if applyTemplateVariables is non-idempotent (e.g. it appends/replaces based on current content), the shard matcher or the user's query can be corrupted, causing queries to hit the wrong shards or fail to parse. Additionally, the shard grouping was computed from the once-interpolated selector, but execution uses a twice-interpolated expression, so grouping and execution can diverge. The two splitting layers must agree on a single interpolation point; as written, the shard path interpolates twice.

findings.title: runSplitQuery mutates the caller's request object (request.queryGroupId) and, via shared target references, the caller's targets
findings.body: Line 303 does `request.queryGroupId = uuidv4()`, mutating the DataQueryRequest passed in by the caller. When runSplitQuery is invoked from runShardSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts:163), the subRequest is a shallow copy `{ ...request, targets }`, so this assignment writes queryGroupId onto the shard-splitting request object as well. Combined with the in-place mutation performed by applyTemplateVariables on the shared target objects (see related finding), the caller's request and targets are modified as a side effect of running a split query. This is a data-integrity hazard: the same request object may be reused by the datasource for subsequent queries (e.g. streaming/refresh), and mutated targets (interpolated expr, step) would then be re-interpolated or sent with stale values. The function should clone the request (`{ ...request, queryGroupId: uuidv4() }`) and ensure targets are not mutated in place.

findings.title: New interpolation test does not cover the shard-splitting double-interpolation path or non-idempotent variables
findings.body: The added test 'Interpolates queries before execution' (lines 75-88) only verifies that runSplitQuery interpolates `$__auto` and `$step` once when called directly. It does not cover the composition with runShardSplitQuery, where targets are interpolated by runShardSplitQuery and then interpolated again by runSplitQuery. There is no test asserting that a query executed through the shard-splitting path is interpolated exactly once, nor a test with a variable whose interpolated value contains `$`-syntax or LogQL special characters (which would expose re-interpolation corruption). The shard test at shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:84-101 uses a mock datasource whose applyTemplateVariables is the real implementation backed by a `replace` stub, but its assertions only check the final expr/step, and the mock's replace is idempotent, so double interpolation would not be detected. A regression test that runs a query with a non-idempotent variable through runShardSplitQuery and asserts the executed expression is interpolated exactly once is missing.

findings.title: Test expectation changed from 1 to 5 applyTemplateVariables calls without verifying per-shard-group interpolation correctness
findings.body: The test 'Interpolates queries before running' (line 110-112) now asserts `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)`. This reflects that interpolation moved from once-per-request (the old interpolateVariablesInQueries call) to once-per-target inside runShardSplitQuery plus additional calls inside runSplitQuery for each shard sub-request. The count of 5 is incidental (depends on shard grouping internals) and the test does not assert that each executed sub-request's expression was interpolated exactly once and not re-interpolated. If runSplitQuery's new interpolation causes double interpolation on this path, this test would still pass because the mock's replacement is idempotent. The test should assert on the executed expressions (which it partially does) with a non-idempotent mock, or explicitly verify single interpolation per executed query.
